newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil new mooring system to cut costs.
newsitem.headline: Statoil new mooring system to cut costs.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) plans to perform deepwater tests using a new mooring system, which could offer savings of 100 to 300 million crowns compared with existing methods, the company's Status Weekly newsletter said on Friday.
A barge will be moored during August in 1,300 metres of water on the Voering plateau in the Norwegian Sea using fibre cables and anchors, which grip the seabed with aid of suction.
It will be the first time taut mooring with such equipment has been employed along the Atlantic Margin, Status Weekly said.

The weight of steel chain traditionally used to moor floating drilling or production units increases greatly in deep water. Fibre cables are expected to cut such loads by up to 2,500 tonnes, Statoil said.
The system also can be used to moor mobile units, which could help to reduce the pressure on rig capacity for deepwater drilling.
